# Process receipts with Slack & Google Drive

**Pattern:** File Processing · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers ocr-&-extraction work end to end across Slack, Google Drive and Notion.

It moves through 14 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. List Changed Docs (Google Drive)
3. Remove Duplicate Documents
4. Download File Content
5. Extract Text from File
6. Attach Chunk Metadata
7. Insert into Vector Store
8. Prepare Documents
9. Chunk with Overlap
10. Document Embeddings
11. Count Indexed Chunks
12. Summarize Run Stats
13. Append Audit Row (Notion)
14. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing ocr-&-extraction work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → List Changed Docs (Google Drive) → Remove Duplicate Documents → Download File Content → Extract Text from File → Attach Chunk Metadata → Insert into Vector Store → Prepare Documents → Chunk with Overlap → Document Embeddings → Count Indexed Chunks → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Drive aligned by hand for ocr & extraction
- Answering ocr-&-extraction questions from your own indexed documents, then replying in Slack
- Ocr & extraction work where "List Changed Docs (Google Drive)" is still a manual step before Slack
- Ocr & extraction work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Drive in step for ocr & extraction, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Google Drive are skipped, across all 16 nodes of this ocr-&-extraction build
- A failed Slack or Google Drive call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 16 nodes in this ocr-&-extraction build
- Fans the same result out to Notion in the same run, for ocr & extraction
- Ocr-&-extraction answers come from your indexed content, not model recall, before reaching Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google AI API key; Google OAuth2; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2; Supabase URL + service key.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Ingestion is a separate workflow from querying because indexing and answering have different triggers, schedules, and failure modes — a slow re-index should never block a live user question. Chunking with overlap (not whole documents) keeps each retrieval hit focused on relevant text instead of dragging in an entire document's unrelated sections.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Change chunkSize and chunkOverlap, then compare retrieval quality back in the query workflow.
2. Add a second file source and normalize both into the same chunk-metadata shape.
3. Swap the embedding model — but change it in both this workflow and the query workflow, since they must match.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Supabase URL + service key**
Supabase → Project Settings → API → URL + service_role key.
_Gotcha:_ Enable the pgvector extension and create the matching table first.

**Google AI API key**
Same Google AI key as the Gemini chat model.
_Gotcha:_ Must match between indexing and querying.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Retrieval returns nothing or irrelevant chunks**
Cause: Index is empty, or indexing and querying used different embedding models.
Fix: Run the ingestion workflow first, and make sure both sides use the identical embedding model.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your ocr & extraction process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole ocr-&-extraction payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
